claim: Single-structure models derived from X-ray data do not adequately account for the inherent, functionally important dynamics of protein molecules.
source: Single-structure models derived from X-ray data do not adequately account for the inherent, functionally important dynamics of protein molecules.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract presenting the motivation for the study.

claim: Ensembles of structures were generated by time-averaged refinement, where local molecular vibrations were sampled by molecular-dynamics (MD) simulation whilst global disorder was partitioned into an underlying overall translation–libration–screw (TLS) model.
source: We generated ensembles of structures by time-averaged refinement, where local molecular vibrations were sampled by molecular-dynamics (MD) simulation whilst global disorder was partitioned into an underlying overall translation–libration–screw (TLS) model.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: Modeling of 20 protein datasets at 1.1–3.1 Å resolution reduced cross-validated Rfree values by 0.3–4.9%.
source: Modeling of 20 protein datasets at 1.1–3.1 Å resolution reduced cross-validated Rfree values by 0.3–4.9%, indicating that ensemble models fit the X-ray data better than single structures.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the study supported by data in Table 1.

claim: Ensemble models fit the X-ray data better than single structures.
source: Modeling of 20 protein datasets at 1.1–3.1 Å resolution reduced cross-validated Rfree values by 0.3–4.9%, indicating that ensemble models fit the X-ray data better than single structures.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the Rfree reduction data.

claim: Most proteins display a well-ordered core.
source: The ensembles revealed that, while most proteins display a well-ordered core, some proteins exhibit a 'molten core' likely supporting functionally important dynamics in ligand binding, enzyme activity and protomer assembly.
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble models.

claim: Some proteins exhibit a 'molten core' likely supporting functionally important dynamics in ligand binding, enzyme activity and protomer assembly.
source: The ensembles revealed that, while most proteins display a well-ordered core, some proteins exhibit a 'molten core' likely supporting functionally important dynamics in ligand binding, enzyme activity and protomer assembly.
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble models with functional interpretation.

claim: Order–disorder changes in HIV protease indicate a mechanism of entropy compensation for ordering the catalytic residues upon ligand binding by disordering specific core residues.
source: Order–disorder changes in HIV protease indicate a mechanism of entropy compensation for ordering the catalytic residues upon ligand binding by disordering specific core residues.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the ensemble refinement results for HIV protease.

claim: Ensemble refinement extracts dynamical details from the X-ray data that allow a more comprehensive understanding of structure–dynamics–function relationships.
source: Thus, ensemble refinement extracts dynamical details from the X-ray data that allow a more comprehensive understanding of structure–dynamics–function relationships.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study results.

claim: There have been experimental observations of dynamic motion in proteins and other biomolecules since the dawn of structural biology.
source: Since the dawn of structural biology there have been experimental observations of dynamic motion in proteins and other biomolecules (Linderstrøm-Lang and Schellman, 1959).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to historical work.

claim: Multiple biophysical methods have firmly established that atomic 'wigglings and jigglings' play an inherent role in both protein structure and function.
source: Multiple biophysical methods have firmly established that such atomic 'wigglings and jigglings' (Feynman et al., 1963) play an inherent role in both protein structure and function; and, in conjunction with high-resolution structures insights into dynamics aid the understanding of biomolecular functions in catalysis, ligand or drug binding and macromolecular interactions.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge with citation.

claim: X-ray diffraction and NMR spectroscopy are presently the primary source of data for high-resolution protein structures.
source: Presently X-ray diffraction and NMR spectroscopy are the primary source of data for high-resolution protein structures.
evidence: This is a statement of current scientific practice.

claim: Microscopy methods may provide information regarding long-range conformational changes.
source: Whereas microscopy methods may provide information regarding long-range conformational changes, NMR characterizes fluctuations at atomic detail.
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities of different methods.

claim: NMR characterizes fluctuations at atomic detail.
source: Whereas microscopy methods may provide information regarding long-range conformational changes, NMR characterizes fluctuations at atomic detail.
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities of NMR.

claim: The number of dynamics studies is relatively sparse in contrast with the wealth of structural information available in the Protein Data Bank (PDB).
source: However, due to the challenging nature of such experiments the number of dynamics studies is relatively sparse in contrast with the wealth of structural information available in the Protein Data Bank (PDB) (Berman et al., 2000).
evidence: This is an observation about the state of the field with citation to PDB.

claim: The majority of entries in the PDB derived from X-ray diffraction data are presented as static, single, structures.
source: The majority of entries in the PDB derived from X-ray diffraction data are presented as static, single, structures, although there is often extensive disorder resulting from protein dynamics and crystal-lattice distortions.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of PDB entries.

claim: There is often extensive disorder in protein crystal structures resulting from protein dynamics and crystal-lattice distortions.
source: The majority of entries in the PDB derived from X-ray diffraction data are presented as static, single, structures, although there is often extensive disorder resulting from protein dynamics and crystal-lattice distortions.
evidence: This is a statement about the nature of disorder in protein crystals.

claim: Extracting atomic fluctuations from diffraction data would dramatically increase the scope for dynamics studies of biomolecules.
source: Extracting atomic fluctuations from these diffraction data would dramatically increase the scope for dynamics studies of biomolecules and potentially reveal atomic details of structure–function–dynamic mechanisms that have previously been obscured.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential impact of the method.

claim: The diffraction data of proteins are affected by multiple sources of disorder, notably arising from atomic vibrations, concerted motions of protein domains and inter-molecular lattice distortions.
source: The diffraction data of proteins are affected by multiple sources of disorder, notably arising from atomic vibrations, concerted motions of protein domains and inter-molecular lattice distortions.
evidence: This is a statement about the sources of disorder in diffraction data.

claim: Structural models of proteins should account for both anisotropic and anharmonic distributions around the mean atomic positions to reproduce the observed Bragg intensities accurately.
source: Structural models of proteins should account for both anisotropic and anharmonic distributions around the mean atomic positions to reproduce the observed Bragg intensities accurately (Vitkup et al., 2002; Furnham et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a statement about modeling requirements with citations.

claim: Explicit modelling of anisotropic and anharmonic distributions in macromolecules using current methods requires extensive parameterization inappropriate for the diffraction quality of a typical protein crystal.
source: However, explicit modelling of such distributions in macromolecules using current methods requires extensive parameterization inappropriate for the diffraction quality of a typical protein crystal.
evidence: This is a statement about limitations of current modeling methods.

claim: Multi-conformer structures represent both anisotropic and anharmonic disorder.
source: Multi-conformer structures represent both anisotropic and anharmonic disorder, but despite numerous attempts at automating the inclusion of minor conformations (DePristo et al., 2004; Levin et al., 2007; Terwilliger et al., 2007; Korostelev et al., 2009; van den Bedem et al., 2009; Lang et al., 2010), 95% of all protein residues in the Protein Data Bank (PDB) (Berman et al., 2000) derived from diffraction data are modelled with a single conformation (Lang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a statement about multi-conformer structures with citations.

claim: 95% of all protein residues in the Protein Data Bank (PDB) derived from diffraction data are modelled with a single conformation.
source: Multi-conformer structures represent both anisotropic and anharmonic disorder, but despite numerous attempts at automating the inclusion of minor conformations (DePristo et al., 2004; Levin et al., 2007; Terwilliger et al., 2007; Korostelev et al., 2009; van den Bedem et al., 2009; Lang et al., 2010), 95% of all protein residues in the Protein Data Bank (PDB) (Berman et al., 2000) derived from diffraction data are modelled with a single conformation (Lang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a statistical fact about PDB entries with citation.

claim: A MD simulation with time-averaged restraints results in a population of structures in which the individual models are interrelated by a Boltzmann-weighted energy function.
source: As opposed to multiple discrete models, a MD simulation with time-averaged restraints (Gros et al., 1990) results in a population of structures in which the individual models are interrelated by a Boltzmann-weighted energy function.
evidence: This is a description of the MD simulation approach with citation.

claim: The time-averaged restraints method was introduced by Torda et al. (1989) and implemented in macromolecular crystallography by Gros et al. (1990).
source: This method introduced by Torda et al. (1989) and implemented in macromolecular crystallography by Gros et al. (1990), showed a reduction in R-value.
evidence: This is a historical statement with citations.

claim: The time-averaged restraints method showed a reduction in R-value.
source: This method introduced by Torda et al. (1989) and implemented in macromolecular crystallography by Gros et al. (1990), showed a reduction in R-value.
evidence: This is a statement about the results of previous work with citations.

claim: Cross-validation revealed chronically over-fitted models in previous time-averaged restraints implementations.
source: However, cross-validation introduced subsequently (Brünger, 1992) revealed chronically over-fitted models (Burling and Brunger, 1994; Clarage and Phillips, 1994; Schiffer et al., 1995).
evidence: This is a statement about problems with previous methods with citations.

claim: The presented ensemble-refinement method restricts the number of structures modelled and thereby prevents over-fitting of the data.
source: Here, we present an ensemble-refinement method that restricts the number of structures modelled and thereby prevents over-fitting of the data.
evidence: This is a description of the new method's approach.

claim: Large-scale motions, attributable to lattice distortions, are modeled by an underlying global disorder model.
source: We model large-scale motions, attributable to, for example, lattice distortions, by an underlying global disorder model.
evidence: This is a description of the modeling approach.

claim: The approach allows MD simulations to sample local atomic fluctuations only, without the need for sampling large-scale global disorder.
source: This approach allows MD simulations to sample local atomic fluctuations only, without the need for sampling large-scale global disorder.
evidence: This is a description of the method's capability.

claim: The method yields reproducible ensembles with improved fit to the X-ray data, as validated by cross validation, Rfree.
source: We show that the method yields reproducible ensembles with improved fit to the X-ray data, as validated by cross validation, Rfree (Brünger, 1992), and stereochemical analyses.
evidence: This is a statement of the study's results.

claim: Analyses of the ensembles show that detailed features are observed indicating atomic fluctuations that may be relevant for the biological function of the macromolecules.
source: Analyses of the ensembles show that detailed features are observed indicating atomic fluctuations that may be relevant for the biological function of the macromolecules.
evidence: This is a statement of the study's findings.

claim: MD simulations were performed in which the model was restrained by a time-averaged X-ray, maximum-likelihood target function.
source: We performed MD simulations, in which the model was restrained by a time-averaged X-ray (Gros et al., 1990), maximum-likelihood (Pannu and Read, 1996; Adams et al., 1997; Murshudov et al., 1997) target function (see 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This is a description of the methodology with citations.

claim: The X-ray restraint optimized 〈Fcalc(hkl)〉 against Fobs(hkl), where 〈Fcalc(hkl)〉 are computed as rolling averages from the structures in the MD trajectory.
source: The X-ray restraint optimized 〈Fcalc(hkl)〉 against Fobs(hkl), where 〈Fcalc(hkl)〉 are computed as rolling averages from the structures in the MD trajectory, with the length of the averaging window determined by the relaxation time τx.
evidence: This is a description of the computational approach.

claim: Prior to the simulations, large-scale disorder was approximated by an overall TLS model derived from the atomic B-factors of the refined single structure.
source: Prior to the simulations we approximated the large-scale disorder by an overall TLS model derived from the atomic B-factors of the refined single structure.
evidence: This is a description of the preprocessing step.

claim: One TLS group per protein molecule or domain was used.
source: Using one TLS group per protein molecule or domain, we iteratively fitted TLS parameters (Schomaker and Trueblood, 1968; Winn et al., 2001) to the atomic B-factors of the protein atoms excluding atoms with large deviations in B-factor from the TLS-derived B-factor (the parameter pTLS described the percentage of atoms included in TLS-fitting; see 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This is a description of the TLS modeling approach with citations.

claim: The TLS model of the protein core excludes the effects of hyper-flexible surface loops.
source: Effectively, this TLS model of the protein core excludes the effects of hyper-flexible surface loops and, hence, describes the global disorder that may be attributed to inter-molecular lattice distortions and overall intra-molecular breathing or domain shifts.
evidence: This is an explanation of what the TLS model represents.

claim: Ensemble refinement was tested using 20 diffraction datasets from the PDB.
source: Ensemble refinement was tested using 20 diffraction datasets from the PDB and started from either the PDB or PDB_REDO (Joosten et al., 2010) structures ('Materials and methods').
evidence: This is a description of the test datasets with citation.

claim: Upper resolution limits of the datasets ranged from 1.1 to 3.1 Å resolution.
source: Upper resolution limits of the datasets ranged from 1.1 to 3.1 Å resolution and structures had 50 to 1,004 amino-acid residues in the asymmetric unit (Table 1).
evidence: This is a description of the dataset characteristics.

claim: Structures had 50 to 1,004 amino-acid residues in the asymmetric unit.
source: Upper resolution limits of the datasets ranged from 1.1 to 3.1 Å resolution and structures had 50 to 1,004 amino-acid residues in the asymmetric unit (Table 1).
evidence: This is a description of the dataset characteristics.

claim: The simulations were run at an effective temperature of 300 K for the protein atoms.
source: The simulations were run at an effective temperature of 300 K for the protein atoms, using a temperature bath (Tbath) slightly below 300 K to allow for heating due to the non-conservative nature of the time-averaged X-ray restraint modulated by its weight wx-ray ('Materials and methods').
evidence: This is a description of the simulation parameters.

claim: Explicitly modelled solvent atoms were added and/or removed intermittently during the simulation dependent on the corresponding electron-density and difference maps.
source: Explicitly modelled solvent atoms were added and/or removed intermittently during the simulation dependent on the corresponding electron-density and difference maps ('Materials and methods').
evidence: This is a description of the solvent modeling approach.

claim: Bulk solvent effects were accounted for by an averaged Flat Bulk-Solvent Model.
source: Bulk solvent effects were accounted for by an averaged Flat Bulk-Solvent Model (Jiang and Brünger, 1994; Afonine et al., 2005) ('Materials and methods').
evidence: This is a description of the bulk solvent modeling with citations.

claim: The parameters pTLS, τx and the Tbath and wx-ray pair were optimized in a grid search resulting in a shallow optimum scored by Rfree.
source: The parameters pTLS, τx and the Tbath and wx-ray pair were optimized in a grid search resulting in a shallow optimum scored by Rfree (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a description of the parameter optimization with reference to a figure.

claim: After a period of equilibration, the trajectory of structures was acquired over an extensive period of time (40 times τx).
source: After a period of equilibration, the trajectory of structures was acquired over an extensive period of time (40 times τx).
evidence: This is a description of the simulation protocol.

claim: The ensemble models yield improved Rfree values for all datasets, ranging in improvement from 0.3% to 4.9% with a mean improvement of 1.8%.
source: The ensemble models yield improved Rfree values for all datasets, ranging in improvement from 0.3% to 4.9% with a mean improvement of 1.8%.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from Table 1.

claim: For dataset 1UOY, the largest improvement in Rfree was observed among the datasets tested.
source: Figure 1B shows the R-values as they developed over the simulation time for a structure with PDB code 1UOY (Olsen et al., 2004), for which the largest improvement in Rfree was observed among the datasets tested (possibly due to the high degree of anisotropic and anharmonic side-chain motion for this case).
evidence: This is a specific observation about one dataset with citation.

claim: The R-values started at a high value and remained high (∼35%) for the individual structures.
source: The R-values started at a high value and remained high (∼35%) for the individual structures, which is in agreement with the observation that the derived global TLS B-factor model is not optimal for fitting a single structure to the data.
evidence: This is an observation from the simulation with interpretation.

claim: Averaging the structure factors over the relaxation time τx of 1 ps dropped the Rwork and Rfree to ∼11% and ∼15% respectively.
source: Averaging the structure factors over the relaxation time τx of 1 ps (corresponding to the rolling average structure factors used in the X-ray restraint) dropped the Rwork and Rfree to ∼11% and ∼15% respectively.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the simulation.

claim: The Rwork and Rfree of the collected ensemble of structures monotonically decreased to 10.3 and 13.7% respectively over the acquisition period of 40 ps.
source: The Rwork and Rfree of the collected ensemble of structures (corresponding to unweighted averaged structure factors) monotonically decreased to 10.3 and 13.7% respectively. over the acquisition period of 40 ps.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the simulation.

claim: The improvement in R-values from the ensemble model with respect to the single-structure model spanned the entire resolution range of the data.
source: The improvement in R-values from the ensemble model with respect to the single-structure model spanned the entire resolution range of the data (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is an observation from the data with reference to a figure.

claim: Acquisition over 40 times τx yielded a highly redundant set of structures.
source: Acquisition over 40 times τx yielded a highly redundant set of structures.
evidence: This is an observation about the simulation output.

claim: The number of structures was reduced by calculating the minimum number of structures required to reproduce the R-value of the trajectory.
source: We reduced the number of structures by calculating the minimum number of structures, that is 167 in the case of 1UOY, required to reproduce the R-value of the trajectory (Figure 1D and 'Materials and methods').
evidence: This is a description of the structure selection procedure with reference to a figure.

claim: Analysis of all 20 datasets showed that ensemble refinement improved the Rfree by between 0.3 and 4.9 percentage points compared to single structures re-refined using the same program package.
source: Analysis of all 20 datasets showed that ensemble refinement improved the Rfree by between 0.3 and 4.9 percentage points compared to single structures re-refined using the same program package, that is Phenix (Afonine et al., 2012), with a mean improvement of 1.8% in Rfree values (Table 1, Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the study with citation and reference to table and figure.

claim: The effect of the starting structure on ensemble refinement was assessed by using alternative refinement programs.
source: The effect of the starting structure on ensemble refinement was assessed by using alternative refinement programs, phenix.refine, Refmac (Vagin et al., 2004), and Buster (Bricogne et al., 2009), to generate varying input models.
evidence: This is a description of a validation test with citations.

claim: No significant differences were observed due to the different starting models.
source: No significant differences were observed due to the different starting models (Tables 3 and 4).
evidence: This is a result from the validation test with reference to tables.

claim: The improvement in Rfree, number of structures in the final ensemble and the averaging time τx tended to increase with resolution.
source: The improvement in Rfree, number of structures in the final ensemble and the averaging time τx tended to increase with resolution (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is an observation about trends in the data with reference to figures.

claim: The optimum values for the parameters pTLS and Tbath are not correlated with resolution.
source: The optimum values for the parameters pTLS and Tbath are not correlated with resolution (Figure 2D,E).
evidence: This is an observation about parameter optimization with reference to figures.

claim: The ensemble models reduced electron-density differences, decreasing rms fluctuations in difference maps by 0 to 41% with an average of 12% improvement.
source: Concomitant with the reduction in R-values, the ensemble models reduced electron-density differences, decreasing rms fluctuations in difference maps by 0 to 41% with an average of 12% improvement (Table 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result with reference to a table.

claim: The difference electron-density maps for the single-structure and ensemble models indicated improvements throughout the asymmetric unit cell.
source: The difference electron-density maps for the single-structure and ensemble models indicated improvements throughout the asymmetric unit cell, as exemplified in Figure 1E.
evidence: This is an observation with reference to a figure.

claim: High-quality experimental phases available to high resolution for 1YTT of mannose-binding protein were used to validate the ensemble-refinement method.
source: We used the high-quality experimental phases available to high resolution for 1YTT of mannose-binding protein (Burling et al., 1996) to validate the ensemble-refinement method.
evidence: This is a description of the validation approach with citation.

claim: The overall correlation coefficient between the electron-density map from the ensemble model and the experimentally phased electron-density map was 0.903.
source: The overall correlation coefficient between the electron-density map from the ensemble model (obtained without experimental phases) and the experimentally phased electron-density map was 0.903, compared with 0.873 and 0.895 for the published and re-refined single structures.
evidence: This is a quantitative validation result.

claim: Real-space correlation coefficients highlighted marked local improvements for flexible residues in particular.
source: Real-space correlation coefficients (Brändén and Jones, 1990) highlighted marked local improvements for flexible residues in particular (Figure 3A) with 11 residues improving by more than 0.1 in correlation coefficient.
evidence: This is a quantitative result with citation and reference to a figure.

claim: 11 residues improved by more than 0.1 in correlation coefficient.
source: Real-space correlation coefficients (Brändén and Jones, 1990) highlighted marked local improvements for flexible residues in particular (Figure 3A) with 11 residues improving by more than 0.1 in correlation coefficient.
evidence: This is a quantitative result with citation and reference to a figure.

claim: The ensemble model contained structural details previously identified in a multiple-model approach by Burling et al. (1996).
source: Moreover, the ensemble model contained structural details previously identified in a multiple-model approach by Burling et al. (1996), as shown for the anisotropic distribution for the side chain of Phe121 (Figure 3C) and diffuse water shells around hydrophobic residues (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a comparison with previous work with citation and reference to figures.

claim: The most occupied water sites in the ensemble correlated with low atomic B-factors for waters in the single-structure model.
source: Figure 3E shows that the most occupied water sites in the ensemble correlated with low atomic B-factors for waters in the single-structure model.
evidence: This is an observation with reference to a figure.

claim: The rms deviations from idealized bond lengths, bond angles and dihedral angles for the re-refined single-structures were 0.010 Å, 1.26° and 15.2° respectively.
source: Averaged over all 20 cases, the rms deviations from idealized bond lengths, bond angles and dihedral angles for the re-refined single-structures were 0.010 Å, 1.26° and 15.2° respectively. (Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result about stereochemistry.

claim: These deviations decreased for the ensemble models by 0.002 Å, 0.26° and 6.6° respectively, when considering the centroids of the observed stereochemical distributions.
source: These deviations decreased for the ensemble models by 0.002 Å, 0.26° and 6.6° respectively, when considering the centroids of the observed stereochemical distributions.
evidence: This is a quantitative result comparing ensemble to single structures.

claim: Taking all fluctuations around the centroids into account, these values increased by 0.002 Å, 0.33° and 4.0° respectively compared to the statistics from single structures.
source: Taking all fluctuations around the centroids (i.e. complete distributions) into account, these values increased by 0.002 Å, 0.33° and 4.0° respectively compared to the statistics from single structures.
evidence: This is a quantitative result about the full distributions.

claim: High-energy conformations occurred transiently and were concentrated in regions of structural flexibility.
source: Figure 6A,B shows that high-energy conformations, as indicated by for example non-favourable Ramachandran φ,ψ-angle combinations, occurred transiently and were concentrated in regions of structural flexibility.
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis with reference to figures.

claim: The ensembles have a similar percentage for 'allowed' and an increased number of 'outliers' compared to the single structures.
source: Counting the most frequent Ramachandran classification for each φ,ψ-angle showed that the ensembles have a similar percentage for 'allowed' and an increased number of 'outliers' compared to the single structures (Figure 6C and Figure 6—source data 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result about Ramachandran statistics with reference to figure.

claim: Lower Rfree values correlate with better quality of the Ramachandran statistics.
source: Similar to Brünger (Brünger, 1992), we observe that lower Rfree values correlate with better quality of the Ramachandran statistics (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is an observation with citation and reference to figure.

claim: The observed atomic distributions are highly reproducible.
source: The robustness of the observed atomic distributions was tested by repeating ensemble refinements 10 times using different random starting velocities. Figure 4A shows that the observed distributions are highly reproducible.
evidence: This is a result from reproducibility testing with reference to figure.

claim: With data extending to 1.5-Å resolution correlations above 0.99 were observed between residue distributions from separate runs.
source: With data extending to 1.5-Å resolution correlations above 0.99 were observed between residue distributions from separate runs.
evidence: This is a quantitative result about reproducibility.

claim: At lower resolutions, the majority of residues showed correlations above 0.95.
source: At lower resolutions, the majority of residues showed correlations above 0.95, with occasionally correlations dropping below 0.8 in very flexible regions (see Figure 4B,C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result about reproducibility with reference to figures.

claim: The presence of non-crystallographic symmetry (NCS) allowed for crystallographically-independent observations of atomic fluctuations in multiple copies of a protein molecule.
source: The presence of non-crystallographic symmetry (NCS) allowed for crystallographically-independent observations of atomic fluctuations in multiple copies of a protein molecule (Figure 7A–C).
evidence: This is a statement about the use of NCS with reference to figures.

claim: Atomic fluctuations were similar both in magnitude and location for related copies in areas not affected by crystal packing.
source: Nevertheless, we observed atomic fluctuations similar both in magnitude and location for related copies in areas not affected by crystal packing (Figure 7B,C; additional cases of NCS are presented in Figure 7—figure supplement 1–4).
evidence: This is an observation from NCS analysis with reference to figures.

claim: Variations in overall disorder arising from packing differences of NCS copies were well accounted for by the applied global TLS models.
source: Apparently, variations in overall disorder arising from packing differences of NCS copies (as indicated by different B-factor distributions) were well accounted for by the applied global TLS models.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the NCS results.

claim: A global increase in disorder present in a dataset collected at ambient temperature vs an isomorphous dataset collected under cryo-conditions was fully accounted for by an increase in global TLS.
source: Similarly, a global increase in disorder present in a dataset collected at ambient temperature vs an isomorphous dataset collected under cryo-conditions was fully accounted for by an increase in global TLS (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is an observation from temperature comparison with reference to figure.

claim: The derived atomic fluctuations are molecular traits.
source: These data indicate that the derived atomic fluctuations are molecular traits and that the global TLS model accounts for overall disorder, which includes for example lattice or packing effects.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results.

claim: Most proteins are characterized by well-ordered residues in the protein core and flexible residue side chains and loops on the outside.
source: Inspection of the obtained ensembles showed that most proteins, as expected, are characterized by well-ordered residues in the protein core and flexible residue side chains and loops on the outside (an example is given in Figure 9A).
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis with reference to figure.

claim: Three cases exhibited marked flexibility of residue side chains on the inside of the molecule.
source: However, three cases exhibited marked flexibility of residue side chains on the inside of the molecule.
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis.

claim: 1BV1 (major birch pollen allergen) has a large forked solvent channel with multiple disordered side chains and a diffuse water network.
source: 1BV1 (Gajhede et al., 1996), major birch pollen allergen, has a large forked solvent channel with multiple disordered side chains and a diffuse water network (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis with citation and reference to figure.

claim: The cavity in 1BV1 is consistent with its putative role as a general plant steroid carrier.
source: The cavity is consistent with its putative role as a general plant steroid carrier (Marković-Housley et al., 2003).
evidence: This is an interpretation with citation.

claim: The flexible internal residues in 1BV1 presumably play a role in binding the diverse ligands.
source: Presumably, the flexible internal residues play a role in binding the diverse ligands.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the structural observation.

claim: 1X6P of PAK pilin has disordered cores.
source: More surprising are the disordered cores in 1X6P of PAK pilin (Dunlop et al., 2005) (Figure 9C) and 3K0N of the enzyme proline isomerase (Fraser et al., 2009) (Figure 9D); in both these cases, the datasets were recorded at ambient temperatures.
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis with citations and reference to figures.

claim: Multiple (16) aliphatic and aromatic side chains are highly flexible, forming a molten core in the pilin molecule.
source: Multiple (16) aliphatic and aromatic side chains are highly flexible, forming a molten core in the pilin molecule.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the ensemble analysis.

claim: The flexible residues in pilin are extremely well conserved in the type IV pilin family.
source: These flexible residues, which are extremely well conserved in the type IV pilin family, create the central interface between the characteristic long α-helix and β-sheet of this protein fold (Hazes et al., 2000).
evidence: This is an observation with citation.

claim: The monomeric pilin structure represents an intermediate molten state, which becomes stabilized upon protomer filament formation.
source: We hypothesize that this monomeric pilin structure represents an intermediate molten state, which becomes stabilized upon protomer filament formation.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the structural observation.

claim: 3K0N of proline isomerase has several (11) aromatic and aliphatic residues that showed large side chain fluctuations, yielding a molten core of the protein structure.
source: The third case with flexible residues on the interior is 3K0N of proline isomerase (Fraser et al., 2009). As with the pilin structure, several (11) aromatic and aliphatic residues showed large side chain fluctuations, yielding a molten core of the protein structure.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the ensemble analysis with citation.

claim: The same protein under cryogenic conditions (3K0M) showed mostly well-ordered side chains in the ensemble.
source: However, the same protein under cryogenic conditions (3K0M) (Fraser et al., 2009) showed mostly well-ordered side chains in the ensemble (Figure 9D, right-hand side), indicating that at cryogenic conditions the molten core has been annealed to its ground state configuration.
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis with citation and reference to figure.

claim: At cryogenic conditions the molten core has been annealed to its ground state configuration.
source: However, the same protein under cryogenic conditions (3K0M) (Fraser et al., 2009) showed mostly well-ordered side chains in the ensemble (Figure 9D, right-hand side), indicating that at cryogenic conditions the molten core has been annealed to its ground state configuration.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the temperature comparison with citation and reference to figure.

claim: The observed flexibility of the core residues at ambient temperature is likely of functional relevance for the enzyme.
source: As discussed in more detail in the next paragraph, the observed flexibility of the core residues at ambient temperature is likely of functional relevance for the enzyme.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results.

claim: The computed ensemble models highlighted a hitherto unnoticed phenomenon of molten cores in folded proteins, which are likely relevant for the biological function of these molecules.
source: Thus, the computed ensemble models highlighted a hitherto unnoticed phenomenon of molten cores in folded proteins, which are likely relevant for the biological function of these molecules.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observations.

claim: NMR spectroscopy has previously revealed specific dynamics for active-site residues of proline isomerase.
source: NMR spectroscopy has previously revealed specific dynamics for active-site residues of proline isomerase (Eisenmesser et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a statement about previous work with citation.

claim: The solvent-exposed residues Arg55 and Met61 in the active site showed disorder in 3K0M.
source: The solvent-exposed residues Arg55 and Met61 in the active site showed disorder in 3K0M (Fraser et al., 2009), where data were collected at 100 K.
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis with citation.

claim: For 3K0N collected at 288 K, a number of additional residues with multiple conformations were observed.
source: For 3K0N collected at 288 K, a number of additional residues with multiple conformations were observed (Figure 8A,B).
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis with reference to figures.

claim: Ensemble refinement of the 288 K data revealed a large number of residue side chains in the core to be flexible.
source: Ensemble refinement of the 288 K data revealed a large number of residue side chains in the core to be flexible.
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis.

claim: The flexibility in the core appears to be linked to the dynamics of active-site residues through the intervening β-sheet.
source: This flexibility in the core appears to be linked to the dynamics of active-site residues through the intervening β-sheet.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural observations.

claim: The main-chain H-bonding network (C=O·HN) of neighbouring β-strands within the sheet was flexible.
source: In particular, the main-chain H-bonding network (C=O·HN) of neighbouring β-strands within the sheet was flexible, as indicated by anisotropy in the C=O bonds of residues 55-62-113-98 (with the largest anisotropy observed for 55 and 62; see Figure 10B).
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis with reference to figure.

claim: Analysis of the side-chain conformations for the active-site residues Arg55, Met61, Ser99 and Phe113 showed a 10% minor conformation for the four active-site residues.
source: Analysis of the side-chain conformations for the active-site residues Arg55, Met61, Ser99 and Phe113 showed a 10% minor conformation for the four active-site residues (Figure 10C), which is in good agreement with NMR relaxation data (see Figure 2 in Eisenmesser et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the ensemble analysis with reference to figure and citation.

claim: Mutation of Ser99 to Thr affects the side-chain distributions and lowers the activity ∼300-fold.
source: Mutation of Ser99 to Thr (>14 Å away from the catalytic Arg55) affects the side-chain distributions and lowers the activity ∼300-fold, similar to an Arg55Lys mutation of the catalytic residue (Eisenmesser et al., 2005; Fraser et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a statement about experimental results with citations.

claim: The ensemble refinement results support the notion that side chain dynamics play a critical role in the enzymatic function of proline isomerase.
source: Thus, the ensemble refinement results support the notion put forward by Eisenmesser et al. and Fraser et al. that side chain dynamics play a critical role in the enzymatic function of proline isomerase and, moreover, expand upon this theme to reveal mechanistic insights arising from the underlying detailed dynamics.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results with reference to previous work.

claim: Ligand binding to HIV protease is known to have marked effects on the enzyme structure.
source: Ligand binding to HIV protease is known to have marked effects on the enzyme structure (Heaslet et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a statement about known effects with citation.

claim: HIV protease exhibited flexible, moldable, substrate-binding pockets in the apo state.
source: As for proline isomerase, HIV protease exhibited flexible, moldable, substrate-binding pockets in the apo state.
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis.

claim: Enthalpic and entropic binding of the ligand with high affinity (KD = 41 pM) reduced the flexibility in the substrate binding pockets.
source: Enthalpic and entropic binding of the ligand with high affinity (KD = 41 pM) (Velazquez-Campoy et al., 2001) reduced the flexibility in the substrate binding pockets by protein–ligand H-bond interactions and van der Waals stacking (Figure 11A,B).
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis with citation and reference to figures.

claim: Upon ligand binding, Asp90 became ordered through H-bonding with the ligand in P2.
source: Upon ligand binding, Asp90 became ordered through H-bonding with the ligand in P2, whereas its dimeric partner lacked a H-bonding partner in P2′ and remained flexible as in the unbound state.
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis.

claim: The canonical aspartic protease catalytic residues, Asp25 of both monomers, became ordered upon ligand binding.
source: The canonical aspartic protease catalytic residues, Asp25 of both monomers, became ordered upon ligand binding.
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis.

claim: Significant changes in dynamics of specific core residues were observed upon ligand binding.
source: Concomitantly, we observed significant changes in dynamics of specific core residues (Figure 11C).
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis with reference to figure.

claim: Some residues, most notably Thr26, 'froze' upon ligand binding.
source: Some residues, most notably Thr26, 'froze' (Thr26 is part of the conserved Asp25-Thr26-Gly-27 sequence).
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis.

claim: The side chains of Cys95 and Leu97 became highly disordered in the bound state, whereas they were relatively ordered in the unbound state.
source: In contrast, the side chains of other residues, most notably Cys95 and Leu97 opposite of Thr26, became highly disordered in the bound state, whereas they were relatively ordered in the unbound state.
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis.

claim: This observation supports NMR data that showed that conformational variability increases upon inhibitor binding for Leu97 amongst others.
source: This observation supports NMR data that showed that conformational variability increases upon inhibitor binding for Leu97 amongst others (Torchia and Ishima, 2003).
evidence: This is a comparison with previous NMR data with citation.

claim: The entropy lost by the catalytic aspartates upon ligand binding is compensated with an increase in disorder of specific core residue side chains.
source: These data suggest that the entropy lost by the catalytic aspartates upon ligand binding is compensated with an increase in disorder of specific core residue side chains.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the ensemble results.

claim: This type of dynamic modulation was also observed for Ca2+ binding to calmodulin, where this effect was dubbed entropy compensation.
source: This type of dynamic modulation was also observed for Ca2+ binding to calmodulin, where this effect was dubbed entropy compensation (Lee et al., 2000).
evidence: This is a comparison with previous work with citation.

claim: The structure ensembles generated by the ensemble refinement method revealed specific core dynamics for HIV protease, in particular a conformational exchange that is likely functionally relevant.
source: Similar to the molten core dynamics for proline isomerase, the structure ensembles generated by the ensemble refinement method revealed specific core dynamics for HIV protease, in particular a conformational exchange that is likely functionally relevant.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the HIV protease analysis.

claim: The development of new small molecule therapeutics is often supported by the use of macromolecular structure, typically X-ray crystallography of complexes between target proteins and drug candidates.
source: The development of new small molecule therapeutics is often supported by the use of macromolecular structure, typically X-ray crystallography of complexes between target proteins and drug candidates.
evidence: This is a statement about drug development practice.

claim: These complexes are typically interpreted as static structures.
source: These complexes are typically interpreted as static structures, and the impact of dynamics, if considered at all, is probed using computational methods.
evidence: This is a statement about current practice.

claim: The new ensemble refinement approach makes it possible to study the role of dynamics in drug–target complexes in the context of the experimental data.
source: Our new ensemble refinement approach makes it possible to study the role of dynamics in drug–target complexes in the context of the experimental data.
evidence: This is a statement about the capability of the method.

claim: Imatinib binds the Abl kinase with high affinity, 37 nM.
source: These compounds bind the Abl kinase with high affinity, 37 nM (Schindler et al., 2000) and 100 nM respectively (Nagar et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a statement about binding affinity with citation.

claim: PD173955 binds the Abl kinase with high affinity, 100 nM.
source: These compounds bind the Abl kinase with high affinity, 37 nM (Schindler et al., 2000) and 100 nM respectively (Nagar et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a statement about binding affinity with citation.

claim: The ensembles provide insights into the flexibility of the protein residues and the ligand moieties in the complex.
source: The ensembles provide insights into the flexibility of the protein residues and the ligand moieties in the complex.
evidence: This is a statement about the information provided by ensembles.

claim: Variable H-bonding interactions were observed for the hydrophilic N-methylpiperazine moiety with the backbone carbonyl atoms of Ile360 and His361.
source: Figure 12A shows the variation in H-bonding observed in Abl kinase–Imatinib. Variable H-bonding interactions were observed for the hydrophilic N-methylpiperazine moiety with the backbone carbonyl atoms of Ile360 and His361.
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis with reference to figure.

claim: The ensemble displayed a well-ordered H-bond between the anilino-NH and Thr315 'gatekeeper' side-chain.
source: In contrast, the ensemble displayed a well-ordered H-bond between the anilino-NH and Thr315 'gatekeeper' side-chain.
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis.

claim: The ordered water network between Glu286, Lys271 and the pyrimidine moiety of Imatinib was reproduced in the ensemble model.
source: Moreover, the ordered water network between Glu286, Lys271 and the pyrimidine moiety of Imatinib (Nagar et al., 2002) was reproduced in the ensemble model (Figure 12B).
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis with citation and reference to figure.

claim: In the Imatinib complex the activation loop, residues 381–402, is highly disordered.
source: In the Imatinib complex the activation loop, residues 381–402, is highly disordered (Figure 12C), which was confirmed by comparison to previously published NMR data (Vajpai et al., 2008).
evidence: This is an observation from the ensemble analysis with citation and reference to figure.

claim: The ensemble models indicate details of tight and highly ordered drug–target interactions on one side vs disordered interactions elsewhere.
source: In general, the ensemble models indicate details of tight and highly ordered drug–target interactions on one side vs disordered interactions elsewhere, which are indicative of less tight interactions, that may suggest which sites to modify in a drug-optimization cycle.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the ensemble results.

claim: Far more structural information can be reliably extracted from protein diffraction data than is achieved to date by traditional single-structure modelling methods.
source: We have shown that far more structural information can be reliably extracted from protein diffraction data than is achieved to date by traditional single-structure modelling methods.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study.

claim: The ensemble refinement method samples distributions that reflect structural details of protein dynamics.
source: Our ensemble refinement method samples distributions that reflect structural details of protein dynamics.
evidence: This is a statement about the method's capability.

claim: The resulting ensemble models provide a more comprehensive description of the molecules.
source: The resulting ensemble models provide a more comprehensive description of the molecules and allow interpretation of the molecular function in terms of both the three-dimensional arrangements of the protein residues and their flexibilities.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of ensemble models.

claim: Ensemble models minimize the risk of structural over-interpretation associated with the seemingly rigid single-structure models.
source: Moreover, ensemble models minimize the risk of structural over-interpretation associated with the seemingly rigid single-structure models.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of ensemble models.

claim: Comparative analyses of protein molecules in different states are very useful for identifying detailed changes in structural dynamics that may be mechanistically relevant for the molecular function.
source: We found comparative analyses of protein molecules in different states to be very useful for identifying detailed changes in structural dynamics that may be mechanistically relevant for the molecular function.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study.

claim: Partitioning large-scale disorder into a global model separates intermolecular variations of protein packing in the crystal from the detailed intra-molecular atomic fluctuations.
source: Partitioning large-scale disorder into a global model separates intermolecular variations of protein packing in the crystal from the detailed intra-molecular atomic fluctuations.
evidence: This is a description of the method's approach.

claim: The X-ray gradient dictates the MD sampling to yield featureless electron-density difference maps.
source: Effectively, the X-ray gradient dictates the MD sampling to yield featureless, (mFobs−DFmodel)exp[iφmodel], electron-density difference maps, while the global disorder model is accounted for by taking BTLS into account when computing the atomic densities.
evidence: This is a description of how the method works.

claim: The ensemble of structures is generated to model the anisotropic and anharmonic electron-density distributions precisely.
source: In this way, the ensemble of structures is generated to model the anisotropic and anharmonic electron-density distributions precisely, while being restrained by the bonded and non-bonded energy terms used in the MD simulation.
evidence: This is a description of what the method achieves.

claim: The separation of global disorder and local atomic fluctuations contrasts the original approach by Gros et al. (1990).
source: The separation of global disorder and local atomic fluctuations contrasts the original approach by Gros et al. (1990), where the MD sampling had to account for both the large scale global disorder and local fluctuations leading to very long relaxation times τx of 16 ps.
evidence: This is a comparison with previous work with citation.

claim: In the current work much shorter relaxation times of 0.25–2 ps can be used, thereby limiting potential over-fitting markedly.
source: In the current work much shorter relaxation times of 0.25–2 ps can be used, thereby limiting potential over-fitting markedly.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of the new method.

claim: The method is applicable to data with a wide range of upper resolution limits.
source: The method is applicable to data with a wide range of upper resolution limits.
evidence: This is a statement about the method's applicability.

claim: Marked improvements in Rfree are seen for datasets ranging from 1.5 to 2.6-Å upper-resolution limit.
source: We see marked improvements in Rfree for datasets ranging from 1.5 to 2.6-Å upper-resolution limit.
evidence: This is a statement about the results.

claim: A detailed interpretation of the ensembles is allowed, supported by the very high local correlations between independent ensemble refinements.
source: A detailed interpretation of the ensembles is allowed, supported by the very high local correlations between independent ensemble refinements.
evidence: This is a statement about the reliability of the method.

claim: At lower resolution limits and for highly disordered loops the local correlation between independent runs drops and detailed interpretation is not feasible.
source: However, at lower resolution limits and for highly disordered loops the local correlation between independent runs drops and detailed interpretation is not feasible.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the method.

claim: The gain in Rfree and the very high local correlations between independent runs indicate a high reliability of the ensemble models.
source: Thus, even though the number of independent parameters in an ensemble model is not clearly defined (and therefore the parameter-to-observation ratio is unclear), the gain in Rfree and the very high local correlations between independent runs indicate a high reliability of the ensemble models.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the validation results.

claim: The method is not a panacea for highly disordered protein regions.
source: However, the method is not a panacea for highly disordered protein regions.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the method.

claim: In the absence of ordered conformations for a certain region of the protein the ensemble refinement will sample diverse conformations in order to prevent the build up of negative peaks in the electron-density difference map.
source: In the absence of ordered conformations for a certain region of the protein (as implicitly defined by the diffraction data) the ensemble refinement will sample diverse conformations in order to prevent the build up of negative peaks in the electron-density difference map.
evidence: This is a description of how the method handles disorder.

claim: Dataset pathologies caused by radiation damage may have confounded effects that obscure the dynamics inherent to the protein molecule.
source: Furthermore, dataset pathologies caused, for example, by radiation damage may have confounded effects that obscure the dynamics inherent to the protein molecule.
evidence: This is a statement about potential limitations.

claim: This modelling method that accounts for inherent protein dynamics is particularly suited to resolve dynamical fluctuations in ordered parts of the protein structure.
source: Thus, perhaps somewhat counter-intuitively, this modelling method that accounts for inherent protein dynamics does not help to resolve structural details of disordered regions, but is particularly suited to resolve dynamical fluctuations in ordered parts of the protein structure.
evidence: This is a statement about the method's strengths.

claim: Ensemble refinement of 20 protein datasets highlighted global dynamics features of protein molecules.
source: Ensemble refinement of 20 protein datasets highlighted global dynamics features of protein molecules.
evidence: This is a summary of the results.

claim: Molten cores may indicate intermediates of protein molecules that function in larger complexes.
source: Most likely, such molten cores may indicate intermediates of protein molecules that function in larger complexes (such as PAK pilin), or alternatively these molten cores support dynamical fluctuations that are needed for ligand binding and enzyme functioning (as for birch pollen allergen and proline isomerase respectively).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the molten core observations.

claim: Molten cores support dynamical fluctuations that are needed for ligand binding and enzyme functioning.
source: Most likely, such molten cores may indicate intermediates of protein molecules that function in larger complexes (such as PAK pilin), or alternatively these molten cores support dynamical fluctuations that are needed for ligand binding and enzyme functioning (as for birch pollen allergen and proline isomerase respectively).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the molten core observations.

claim: The ensembles show details of specific order–disorder transitions between active site and core residues that suggest a mechanism of entropy compensation to support the enzymatic activity.
source: Furthermore, the ensembles show details of specific order–disorder transitions, or conformational exchanges, between active site and core residues (as for HIV protease in the unbound and bound state) that suggest a mechanism of entropy compensation to support the enzymatic activity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the HIV protease results.

claim: The difference in dynamics observed between the ensembles of proline isomerase at cryo and ambient temperatures indicates that flash freezing of a crystal anneals local conformational fluctuations.
source: The difference in dynamics observed between the ensembles of proline isomerase at cryo and ambient temperatures indicates that flash freezing of a crystal anneals local conformational fluctuations and thereby removes protein dynamics that may be functionally relevant.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the temperature comparison.

claim: Flash freezing of a crystal removes protein dynamics that may be functionally relevant.
source: The difference in dynamics observed between the ensembles of proline isomerase at cryo and ambient temperatures indicates that flash freezing of a crystal anneals local conformational fluctuations and thereby removes protein dynamics that may be functionally relevant.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the temperature comparison.

claim: This new method of modelling X-ray diffraction data reveals a wealth of detailed information about the dynamics of biomolecules that complements the high-resolution structural information already available from the crystallographic experiment.
source: In conclusion, this new method of modelling X-ray diffraction data reveals a wealth of detailed information about the dynamics of biomolecules that complements the high-resolution structural information already available from the crystallographic experiment.
evidence: This is a concluding statement about the method's contribution.

claim: In depth understanding of structure–dynamics in biomolecules will enhance our insights into the molecular mechanisms that underlie biological processes.
source: In depth understanding of structure–dynamics in biomolecules will enhance our insights into the molecular mechanisms that underlie biological processes.
evidence: This is a statement about the broader impact of the work.
